material_facts: The accused is a 45-year-old businessman with no prior criminal record.
Charged under Section 420 and Section 406 IPC related to a property transaction dispute.
Investigation is complete and chargesheet has been filed.
Accused has surrendered his passport voluntarily.
Accused has deep roots in the community and has been cooperating with the investigation.
The accused has already spent 45 days in custody.
prosecution_questions: Is bail appropriate when the accused is alleged to have misappropriated a significant sum of money?
Should the accused remain in custody to prevent potential disposal of assets?
defense_questions: Whether bail should be granted when investigation is complete and charge sheet filed?
Can liberty be denied solely on gravity of accusation without considering individual circumstances?
analysis.case_summary: The accused, a businessman with no prior record, seeks bail in a property transaction dispute after being charged with cheating and breach of trust, arguing it is a civil matter given criminal color.

precedents.case_name: LAVE SH V. STATE (NCT OF DELHI)
precedents.text: Section 438 of the CrPC allows a person to apply for anticipatory bail when they apprehend arrest for a non-bailable offence.
precedents.quote: in a non-bailable offence if a person has reason to believe that he may be arrested, he is free to apply to the High Court

precedents.case_name: Jai Prakash Singh v. State of Bihar & Anr.
precedents.text: Anticipatory bail can be granted only in exceptional circumstances where there is a prima facie view that the accused is falsely implicated and would not misuse liberty.
precedents.quote: Anticipatory bail can be granted only in exceptional circumstances where the court is prima facie of the view that the applicant has falsely been enroped in the crime and would not misuse his liberty.
precedents.reasoning: While it discusses anticipatory bail, it highlights the importance of individual circumstances which can be related to the current case.

adverse_precedent.case_name: Jai Prakash Singh v. State of Bihar & Anr.
adverse_precedent.text: A promptly lodged FIR is a vital and valuable piece of evidence assuring the veracity of the informant’s version.
adverse_precedent.quote: Promptness in filing the FIR gives certain assurance of veracity of the version given by the informant/complainant.
